vuln_id: h2o HTTP/2 post-END_STREAM DATA null callback / ARVO arvo:2623

project.name: h2o
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected for this trace is the ARVO workspace checkout at `77d5f596ec400fb49fecf2395addcc27d4a1d211`; its line map for `lib/http2/connection.c`, `lib/core/proxy.c`, `lib/common/http1client.c`, `lib/common/socket/evloop.c.h`, `lib/handler/proxy.c`, and `fuzz/driver.cc` matches the statements cited below. Sample metadata separately records `b808e2809377cf8ca34a491f3f9280c7a1815ce3` / `56204921b666cfb237f0579a603a946756a1559b` as the vulnerable/fixed commits.

bug_description.original: In streaming body mode, the system does not send an error when receiving data after end_of_stream.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 131-byte witness file for `h2o-fuzzer-http2` is the exact input consumed by the harness: the HTTP/2 client preface, one HEADERS frame on stream 13 whose HPACK block later decodes to `/reproxy-test/`, three 4-byte DATA frames on the same stream, the harness delimiter `\n--MARK--\n`, and one trailing `0x20` byte after that delimiter. `fuzz/driver.cc` writes only the bytes before each marker as a packet, so the trailing space remains in the file but is not forwarded as another packet. In the staged vulnerable checkout at `77d5f596ec400fb49fecf2395addcc27d4a1d211`, `/reproxy-test` is registered as a reverse-proxy path with `has_body_stream = 1`. `handle_headers_frame` installs `stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb = write_req_chunk` for the new stream, and the first DATA chunk enables streaming-body handling and starts reverse-proxy request processing. That proxy path can later swap the callback slot to `frontend_write_req_chunk` in `lib/core/proxy.c:618`, but only from the deferred upstream `on_connect` callback queued through `h2o_socket_notify_write`; `parse_input` keeps consuming the already-buffered staged HEADERS and DATA frames before that later event-loop turn occurs. The witness's second DATA frame therefore still dispatches to `write_req_chunk`, and because its flags byte includes `END_STREAM`, `write_req_chunk` clears `stream->req._write_req_chunk_done` and `stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb` to record that no more request body callbacks should occur. When `handle_data_frame` processes the following DATA frame on the same stream, `stream->state` is still `H2O_HTTP2_STREAM_STATE_RECV_BODY`, but the vulnerable guard checks only stream state and not whether `_write_req_chunk.cb` is NULL. It therefore dispatches the extra DATA through a NULL callback pointer at `lib/http2/connection.c:636`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer null-PC SEGV. The staged fix closes this state-machine gap by rejecting DATA when `_write_req_chunk.cb` is NULL and, for the alternate proxy-frontend arm, explicitly nulling that callback when END_STREAM is seen after the slot has already been swapped.

source.description: First project parser step that decodes the attacker-controlled HEADERS frame, materializing the HPACK block and frame flags that open the HTTP/2 request stream later driven into the vulnerable body-handling path.
source.value_from: After the HTTP/2 client preface, the staged witness contains a HEADERS frame on odd stream id 13 with no END_STREAM flag. `handle_headers_frame` decodes that attacker-controlled frame and passes its HPACK block forward to `handle_incoming_request`, where the request target later materializes as `/reproxy-test/`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The END_STREAM bit on the witness's second DATA frame is converted into the `is_end_stream` callback argument at the body-callback dispatch site. Because the deferred proxy callback swap has not run yet, this call still targets `write_req_chunk`, and the attacker-controlled flag drives that function's callback-clearing branch.

root_cause.description: The DATA-frame rejection logic checks only whether the stream left `RECV_BODY`; it does not also reject the case where the request-body callback slot has already been cleared after END_STREAM. The fix extends this condition to `stream->state != H2O_HTTP2_STREAM_STATE_RECV_BODY || !stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb`.

sink.description: Source-grounded sink that explains the saved null-PC crash: the later DATA frame is dispatched through `stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb` after `write_req_chunk` has already cleared that function pointer to NULL.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace has no symbolized project frames, only `SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000000`, `pc 0x000000000000`, and `READ`. This direct callback dispatch is the concrete project sink that explains a zero-page call target on the witnessed post-END_STREAM DATA path.

parser_admitted.description: After the HEADERS block is parsed successfully and the request is not header-terminated, the stream enters `RECV_BODY`. That admits subsequent DATA frames on this stream into the vulnerable request-body path.

fine_trace.note: Decodes the attacker-controlled HEADERS frame for stream 13 after the HTTP/2 preface. This materializes the HPACK header block and the frame flags that determine whether the request expects later DATA frames.

Preparing the new stream installs `write_req_chunk` as the initial request-body callback. Because the HEADERS frame does not carry END_STREAM, the connection also allocates a request-body buffer so later DATA frames stay on this callback-driven body path.

Parses the decoded HPACK block into `stream->req`. The witness header block materializes `/reproxy-test/` as the request target, which maps to the reverse-proxy handler whose `has_body_stream` flag is 1.

On the first DATA chunk, `h2o_get_first_handler` resolves step 3's `/reproxy-test/` request to the reverse-proxy handler. That enables streaming-body handling by installing `write_req_chunk_done` and starting request processing while the body is still being received.

The exact witness places the HEADERS frame and all three DATA frames before the first `MARKER`, so one read leaves them together in `conn->sock->input` and `parse_input` keeps decoding until that buffer is empty. The reverse-proxy path started in step 4 can later replace `stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb` with `frontend_write_req_chunk`, but only after `h2o_socket_notify_write` queues upstream `on_connect` on `_statechanged` and a later `evloop_do_proceed` promotes it, so the callback slot is still the step-2 `write_req_chunk` when the second DATA frame is handled.

On the witness's second DATA frame on stream 13, `handle_data_frame` still calls the original `write_req_chunk` callback identified in step 5 and forwards the frame's END_STREAM bit as `is_end_stream`. That attacker-controlled flag is what marks the streamed body complete.

Because streaming mode was already active and step 6 supplied a nonzero `is_end_stream`, `write_req_chunk` detaches both the done callback and the request-body callback. This marks the request body closed but does not change `stream->state` here.

When the witness's third DATA frame arrives on the same stream, the vulnerable rejection logic checks only whether the stream left `RECV_BODY`. It does not also reject `!stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb`, so post-END_STREAM DATA is treated as valid even though step 7 has already cleared the callback slot. The fix adds that missing callback-null disjunct to this condition.

The third DATA frame reaches the same callback dispatch site, but step 7 has already set `stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb` to NULL. The indirect call therefore jumps to `pc=0x0`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000000` with `READ` and no symbolized project frame.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged diff adds the missing `!stream->req._write_req_chunk.cb` rejection in `handle_data_frame`, which stops the witnessed third DATA frame before the sink. It also nulls `_write_req_chunk.cb` inside `frontend_write_req_chunk` for the alternate reverse-proxy arm where the callback slot has already been swapped before END_STREAM is seen.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged reproduction_report.json and sanitizer_trace.txt

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Partially. AddressSanitizer only reported `pc=0x0`, `<unknown module>`, and a zero-page READ, but fine-trace step 9 is the concrete NULL callback dispatch on the same post-END_STREAM DATA path and is the first project sink that explains that signature.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Partially. The saved trace contains no symbolized project frames, only the final null-PC SEGV. The source path is nevertheless closed by the staged code: `handle_headers_frame` installs `write_req_chunk`, the first DATA frame starts reverse-proxy streaming-body processing, `parse_input` consumes the buffered staged frames before the deferred proxy `on_connect` path can swap the callback to `frontend_write_req_chunk`, the second DATA frame's END_STREAM clears `_write_req_chunk.cb`, and the third DATA frame reaches the same call site with that slot NULL.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The witness HEADERS select `/reproxy-test/`, the first DATA frame enables streaming-body proxy handling, the buffered second DATA frame still reaches `write_req_chunk`, its END_STREAM bit clears `_write_req_chunk.cb`, and the later DATA frame reaches `handle_data_frame` without the missing callback-null guard, causing the sink call through that now-NULL function pointer.

format.name: h2o-fuzzer-http2 staged HTTP/2 client byte stream
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 131-byte file consumed by `h2o-fuzzer-http2`: an HTTP/2 client preface, one HEADERS frame on stream 13 whose encoded header block contains `/reproxy-test/`, then three 4-byte DATA frames on the same stream with flags bytes `0x20`, `0xff` (including `END_STREAM`), and `0x20`, followed by the harness delimiter `\n--MARK--\n` and one trailing `0x20` byte. `fuzz/driver.cc` writes bytes only up to each marker, so that final space remains in the file but is not forwarded as another packet. No broader input class beyond this exact witnessed post-END_STREAM DATA sequence is claimed.
